People's Majlis

Committee Minutes of the People's Majlis

17th Meeting of the Social Affairs Committee

20 October 2026

Venue of the meeting: New Building of the People's Majlis (Committee Room 12)

Start time: 10:30

{Presiding: Chair of the Committee; Member for Central Maafannu constituency, Asma Rasheed}

Chair speaking:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. 17th meeting of the Social Affairs Committee. Venue: Committee Room 12. Date: 20 October 2026, Tuesday. Time: 10:30. All members of the committee who have come to the committee today so far are present. Member for West Maafannu constituency Musthafa Ibrahim, Member for Kaashidhoo constituency Munthazim Ibrahim, Member for Nilandhoo constituency Fathimath Sauda, Member for South Thinadhoo constituency Mohamed Alsan, Member for Komandoo constituency Mohamed Ibrahim, Member for Naifaru constituency Yaaseen Abdulla, sorry! Excuse me! He has not come yet. Member for Dhaandhoo constituency Mohamed Fazeel, Member for South Mahchangolhi constituency Musthafa Hussain, Member for North Galolhu constituency Mohamed Ibrahim, Member for Addu Meedhoo constituency not present. Issues relating to the bills and resolutions submitted to the committee. Extending the deadline for the bill on the 1st amendment to Law No. 4/2012 (Thalassaemia Control Act), sent back by the President for the People's Majlis to reconsider. The deadline expired on 31 August 2026.

Member for North Galolhu constituency Mohamed Ibrahim speaking:
Our days keep passing by like this, and that is a very sad thing. I think [?] the biggest, perhaps the reason hatred arises towards us, towards the Members of this Majlis, is because things are like this. Because these things here get stuck, no one knows what is happening, and a long time passes. I am sure that a great many issues I brought here are stuck. I really want to point that out. I don't think things will get done if they are done this way. I don't see it getting done. It gets done when we try to do it. Thank you, Chair.

Chair speaking:
I would like to say something to you. If you schedule three a day [unclear], the members here also have other committees. So, we also have recesses. You also have recesses.

Again, after a recess, it has only now reopened. We are now proceeding with a plan to attend to everything you have. Thank you very much.

Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim speaking:
I propose extending the deadline for the bill on the 1st amendment to Law No. 4/2012 (Thalassaemia Control Act), sent back by the President for the People's Majlis to reconsider, until 30 November.

Member for Nilandhoo constituency Fathimath Sauda speaking:
I second the proposal made by the Vice Chair.

Chair speaking:
Members in favour of proceeding as proposed by Vice Chair Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim, West Maafannu constituency, and seconded by Fathimath Sauda, Nilandhoo constituency, please vote. (Voting) Passed unanimously. Reviewing issue submitted to the committee. 1.2- Extending the deadline for the resolution submitted by the Member for North Galolhu constituency, Mohamed Ibrahim, noting that foreigners married to Maldivians and living in the Maldives do not receive Aasandha services, in order to find out the views of Members of the People's Majlis on the matter. The deadline expired on 2 October 2026.

Member for North Galolhu constituency Mohamed Ibrahim speaking:
What I think is that you should make a decision on this. You also make decisions on the other matters here. Make a decision on this. Thank you very much.

Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim speaking:

Thank you. Before actually extending the deadline for the resolution submitted by the Member for North Galolhu constituency, Mohamed Ibrahim, noting that foreigners married to Maldivians and living in the Maldives do not receive Aasandha services, in order to find out the views of Members of the People's Majlis on the matter, there is something I want to say. One thing is that this is work we in the Social Affairs Committee have done as very important work. Work on which a great deal of time has been spent. And letters were sent to some government institutions at the time to obtain certain information we had identified. They were sent to IGMH, to Immigration, to the Family Court and such places. Looking at the information received, I want to point out at this opportunity that in reality we have still not received from those places the level of information we actually need to make a decision, to determine a course. There are also problems in the information sent by the Family Court. There are ways in which it is somewhat difficult for us to make a decision by looking at that data. Immigration is the same. Just looking at that data; for example, after how many years would we give it to a person. If so, how many people are currently in the Maldives who have reached that many years. Or how many marriages there are in the Maldives, how long it has been since those marriages took place and they have been living here. We actually sent the letters to find out many things like this. Having sent them, the information we received is actually not that clear. It is not clear. At the same time, I want to point out that we actually saw the presentation submitted by the honourable member who brought this issue to this committee a short while earlier, before coming to the committee. In that presentation too, the honourable member has pointed out that there are a great many problems in that data. So, is that information not available in the Maldives at those institutions, or what is happening. To put it another way, are we running a country; the information has come in a way that raises questions for us to that level, actually. So, I noticed that it is somewhat more serious than being able to quickly decide something just by looking at the information received. When asked to provide information, is part of the information sent to us held back

when it is sent to the People's Majlis. Or do they not have that data properly maintained. If so, that is in reality a very big problem, not just now! It comes in connection with this matter. I am saying this on the recording precisely because I have concerns. That is, when asked to send information, the information sent does not even state who the person is, who from which country they are married to, what age the person is, what gender the person is; we received the information in this form. So, one option for us is, as I believe, to extend this deadline and get to the point where we bring those officials here and talk to them. We now also need to check whether correct information is not being provided to us. That is a legal offence. So, I propose that this too be taken to 30 November, but working on it at a somewhat faster speed, and proceeding by verifying that information even if by bringing those people in; I propose 30 November as the deadline. And at the same time, as I said, to proceed by bringing those people in and talking to them in order to verify that information. Thank you.

Member for Dhaandhoo constituency Mohamed Fazeel speaking:
In seconding the proposal made by the honourable Vice Chair, the honourable Vice Chair said some very good things. That is, only when we get this data will we know how many foreigners in the Maldives are married to Maldivians. Only once that is known can we do this. So, this cannot proceed unless the information that needs to be obtained is obtained.

Chair speaking:
I put to the vote as proposed by honourable member Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim, West Maafannu constituency, and seconded by Member for Dhaandhoo constituency Mohamed Fazeel. (Voting) Unanimously

passed. Thank you. Today's meeting is now concluded. We will do the rest after scheduling a time tomorrow.
